name: columns
label: Two columns
description: Two components side by side on one slide, at a ratio you choose.
purpose: Use when two components make one point together: a chart and what it means, before and after, a list beside a table.
skeleton:

- A point
- Another point

heading.description: The slide's title, above both panes. It makes the point; the panes support it.

pane.description: Two panes. Each opens with `<!-- _pane: component -->` (optional; default `content`) and an optional `### title`, a short label naming what the pane holds.

whenToUse.title: A chart and what it means
whenToUse.body: Put the evidence in one pane and the reading of it in the other: a `bar` beside a `list`, a `table` beside a `content` pane. The slide's `##` states the conclusion both panes support.

whenToUse.title: Before and after
whenToUse.body: Two `###` titles with no markers make two text panes: the quickest way to set two states side by side.

whenToUse.title: An unequal pair
whenToUse.body: Give the pane that needs room the larger share: `columns ratio-60-40`, `columns ratio-35-65`. Shares run 25 to 75 in 5% steps.

antiPatterns.title: Two unrelated points
antiPatterns.body: Two panes are one argument. If the halves say different things, make two slides.

antiPatterns.title: A binary decision with a verdict
antiPatterns.body: Weighing two options and landing a recommendation is `split-compare`, whose verdict card this layout does not have.

antiPatterns.title: Three or more things
antiPatterns.body: A pane layout holds two panes. Three parallel items are `cards-grid` or `compare-prose`.

related.name: rows
related.when: the two components are wide and read better stacked

related.name: split-panel
related.when: one featured element beside supporting points, not two components

related.name: compare-prose
related.when: two or three co-equal options in prose

commonMistakes.fix: A `##` starts a new slide. Use `###` for a pane's title and `####` for a heading inside a pane.

commonMistakes.mistake: Naming a component in the layout's `_class` (`_class: columns bar`).
commonMistakes.fix: Each pane names its own component: `<!-- _pane: bar -->` above the pane's `###`.

stressDoc.summary: A list beside a four-column table at 40/60, with the slide's Key Insight.
